ledger.claim: The platform's own telemetry settles the route question, and it settles it the rider's way: the code-computed excess of the trace over the 17.3 km optimal route is 0.11 km and 0.64%, below both POL-RD-01 gates (0.8 km absolute and 20%), on a trace of 187 fixes at a 10-second interval with 100% coverage and no gaps. Under POL-RD-01 the trace figure of 17.41 km governs, so the trip_record's rounded 17.4 km may not be cited for the threshold test. No deviation exists on this trip, and the customer-service assertion that the driver detoured is contradicted by the platform's own data — precisely as the rider says.

This trip's clean trace is not an outlier, and the rider's account of the driver is consistent with his own record: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250 — the two fields POL-RD-06 names, and, under POL-GEN-01, the only profile fields citable for that test. That is far below both the 3-flag count and the 0.05 ratio the clause tests, so no POL-RD-06 pattern exists and no uplift or conduct referral is available against this driver.

The rider's dispute is about the price, not the route. fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and fare_breakdown.quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11's upfront-quote protection cannot run and no artifact in this bundle states the fare the rider was actually quoted. The only price reference on the record is trip_record.optimal_route_source, which records that the rider requested RYDE_X, that the platform dispatched RYDE_TAXI, and that an "estimate 22-26" was shown at booking — while the metered total charged was 26.33, above the top of that range. The rider does not say the meter arithmetic is wrong; she says she was billed for a product she did not select, and nothing in this bundle answers that.

The contested total is driven by time, not distance: the meter charged 31 minutes against a platform optimal of 23 minutes, and those 8 extra minutes at the fare model's own 0.28 per minute are 2.24 of the 26.33. The artifact that could speak to those minutes is not on file — EV-ADVIS-00511-01 is a MISSING traffic advisory carrying weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, disclosed here as POL-GEN-02(1) requires — so POL-RD-03's exoneration cannot be run on this record, and the figures actually billed stand unexplained, which POL-RD-13 requires the tribunal to record.

ledger.claim: The rider carries no adverse profile inference on this bundle: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0 — the two fields POL-RD-08 names, and, under POL-GEN-01, the only citable ones for that test — so the heightened-corroboration condition (4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated) does not attach, and no other field on the profile may be turned into a finding against her.

No route deviation is established on this trip. The governing trace measures 17.41 km against an optimal route of 17.3 km, an excess of 0.11 km, which is 0.64% of the optimal. POL-RD-01 requires both that the excess exceed 20% of optimal_distance_km and that it exceed 0.8 km in absolute terms; both tests fail, and where either fails the clause is explicit that no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION 'however the rider characterises the trip'. The rider's own account agrees: 'The DRIVER did nothing wrong, he followed the navigation the whole way.'

The derivation on the driver's own trace returns status 'no deviation' after testing the excess against the clause's four thresholds - 0.8 km and 20% for establishment, 8.0 km and 50% for materiality - and the measured excess approaches none of them. POL-RD-01's trace-governs rule is satisfied whichever figure is used: gps_trace.trace_distance_km of 17.41 km governs, and trip_record.actual_distance_km of 17.4 km is a rounded convenience copy that may not be cited for the threshold test. Neither figure clears the gate.

Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-02 does not run: by its own terms it applies only 'where a deviation is established under POL-RD-01 and no exculpatory clause fully excuses it'. The ledger's precomputed recomputed_fare of 24.015 is an arithmetic output of the fare model sitting inert in the derived block, not an entitlement, and the fare model on this trip is METERED - so there is no route-deviation refund route open at all.

The rider cannot reach ESCALATE by way of trace integrity. POL-RD-07(a) to (c) mark a trace impaired for policy purposes only on a gap over 90 seconds, a straight-line jump over 500 m, or a sustained sampling interval over 30 seconds. This trace fails all three limbs - gaps is empty with max_gap_sec 0.0, the interval is 10 seconds, and 187 fixes cover the segment at 100% coverage - so POL-RD-10(3) cannot fire and there is no corroboration defect for the rider to build on.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show, citing evidence, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired gps_trace. She has the cleanest possible trace - COMPLETE, weight_multiplier 1.0, 100% coverage, no gaps - and it records 0.11 km of excess. The burden is not discharged, the driver is never put to proof on any exculpatory clause, and no artifact she cites supplies the missing excess.

The rider's separate grievance, that the actual fare was above the 22-26 estimate shown at booking, has no remedy in this policy. POL-RD-11 makes a booking figure binding only where fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is non-null; here the fare model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so there is no distance-or-time refund route outside a POL-RD-01 deviation, and none is established.

There is no billing-integrity defect to refund under POL-RD-09(4), the one correction available whether or not a deviation exists, and no off-route pass-through to correct under POL-RD-09(2) because no exoneration arises. The ledger carries no ERP gantries at all (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.00), no airport surcharge (0.00, and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport), and no charge line without a counterpart in the trip record. The metered arithmetic checks out line by line: base 3.80 plus 17.4 km at 0.75 = 13.05 plus 31.0 min at 0.28 = 8.68 plus 0.80 platform fee = 26.33 charged.

No repeat-deviation pattern exists to uplift the remedy or to refer. POL-RD-06's trigger is not even reached, because this trip records no MATERIAL deviation, and the only profile test the clause permits fails on both limbs in any event: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0, where the clause requires 3 or more, and 0 over driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250 is 0.00, where the clause requires 0.05 or more with at least 40 trips. No FULL_REFUND uplift under POL-RD-06(b) and no conduct referral under POL-RD-06(c) follow.

The record holds no traffic advisory. EV-ADVIS-00511-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - 'no advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window' - and I disclose that impairment rather than rely on the artifact. It costs the driver nothing: he asserts no external traffic cause ('Meter fare, standard route'), so the road-naming, validity-window and corridor-matching comparison POL-RD-03 requires cannot be run and neither POL-RD-03 nor POL-RD-13 supplies the rider anything. Because the driver invokes no exculpatory clause against a cited artifact, the POL-RD-10(5) escalation trigger is not engaged by the empty advisory slot either.

The outcome that follows is NO_ACTION, and under POL-GEN-03 that is the driver's outcome on a rider-filed dispute: NO_ACTION leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status and fare_breakdown.refund_issued_sgd exactly as they are, and never means 'restore the charge'. The status here is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the state that stands is the metered fare the driver earned - the contested 26.33 SGD retained, not reversed.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties — the rider and the driver — this is the ruling on dispute DSP-00511, a route-deviation claim over SGD 26.33.

The route question is settled by the platform's own telemetry, and it settles in the driver's favour. The governing trace, EV-GPS-00511 (weight 1.0; COMPLETE; 100% coverage; 187 fixes at a 10-second interval; no gaps; max_gap_sec 0.0), measures 17.41 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff. The booked optimal route on EV-TRIP-00511 is 17.3 km. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure the governing one, so the trip record's rounded 17.4 km may not be used for the threshold test. The excess is 0.11 km, or 0.64% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is both above 0.8 km and above 20%; neither test passes, so no deviation exists on this trip and POL-RD-02 (the optimal-route fare recomputation) never runs. The 24.0150 recomputed_fare, and the 2.35 payable figure resting on it in the fare ledger's derived block, are arithmetic outputs of the fare model sitting inert — not entitlements — because the clause that would make them payable requires an established deviation. That disposes of the customer-service assertion that the driver detoured: it is contradicted by the platform's own data.

The driver-profile consequences also fall away. EV-DPROF-00511 shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against 250 completed trips in 90 days, far below POL-RD-06's tests of 3 flags or a 0.05 ratio with at least 40 trips, so no repeat-pattern uplift and no driver-conduct referral arise.

The rider's two remaining grievances have no remedy in this policy, and I record why. First, the product mismatch: the trip record's optimal_route_source shows she requested RYDE_X and the platform dispatched RYDE_TAXI, and this was a METERED taxi trip; the route-deviation clauses contain no entitlement for the platform's choice of product. Second, the price: fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so POL-RD-11's upfront-quote protection cannot run, and the 'estimate 22-26' mentioned in optimal_route_source is not a quoted fare. Nor is there a billing-integrity defect: charged_total 26.33 = base 3.80 + 17.4 km x 0.75 (13.05) + 31.0 min x 0.28 (8.68) + 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP, toll or surcharge line to refund under POL-RD-09, and every line has a counterpart in the trip record. The rider's related point — that the 31 charged minutes exceed the 23-minute optimal and the missing advisory leaves those minutes unaccounted for — does not change the outcome: POL-RD-01 measures deviation by distance only, that test passes, and POL-RD-13 supplies no correction where no party asserts a traffic cause and no excess meets the threshold.

The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00511-01, status MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT) does not escalate this case. No party asserts an external traffic cause — the driver says only 'Meter fare, standard route' — so POL-RD-03 cannot be invoked by anyone and POL-RD-13's comparison is never engaged; the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction in it, and it does not touch the distance test that decides this case. The trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a) to (c), so POL-RD-10(3) does not fire, and no other POL-RD-10 trigger is met: the trip identifiers match across all three instruments, the timestamps agree, and no refund figure approaches the ceiling.

My confidence is 0.95, capped by the weight-1.0 GPS trace that carries the deciding fact (no deviation), with the weight-1.0 fare ledger carrying the standing of the charge.

The disputed SGD 26.33 is not refunded. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION is party-relative: on this rider-filed dispute it leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00 exactly as they are. No referral is made, because no clause produces one on these facts.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
